title: Distinct (Phospho)proteomic Landscapes of PIK3CA Mutants Reveal Insulin-Mediated Reactivation of PI3K Pathway and Adaptive MAPK Signaling
projectDescription: Oncogenic mutations in p110α subunit of phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase (PI3K), primarily H1047R in the kinase domain and E545K in the helical domain, induce constitutive PI3K/AKT pathway activation, driving tumor progression. Isoform-specific inhibitors such as alpelisib have been developed, but their clinical efficacy is often compromised by on-target metabolic side effects, particularly hyperglycemia and insulin feedback that reactivates PI3K signaling. To better understand the signaling response in PI3K mutants and insulin-mediated tumor resistance, using MCF10A epithelial cells harboring PI3K hotspot mutations (H1047R or E545K), we conducted comprehensive proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses under varying conditions—alpelisib treatment, insulin stimulation, and their combination. We observed mutation specific responses in growth kinetics, proteome states, and dynamic signaling response. We observed that insulin effectively rescues mutant cells from alpelisib-induced inhibition through the reactivation of PI3K pathway and the adaptive reprogramming, especially activation of the MAPK pathways. These findings indicate that combination therapies targeting both the PIK3CA mutation and MAPK pathways may be necessary to overcome challenges faced by PI3Kα inhibitors and achieve more durable clinical responses.
sampleProcessingProtocol: The breast epithelial cells (MCF10A) and the mutant human breast cancer cells, MCF10A PI3Kα (E545K/+) and MCF10A PI3Kα (H1047R/+) were bought from Fisher Scientific (PA, United States). All the MCF10A cells were maintained in regular medium, including Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium/Nutrient Mixture F-12 (DMEM/F-12, Thermo Fisher Scientifc, PA, United States) with 5% horse serum (Invitrogen, CA, United States), 10 µg/ml insulin (Sigma, MA, United States), 0.5 µg/ml hydrocortisone (Sigma, MA, United States), 0.1 µg/ml cholera toxin (Sigma, MA, USA) and 20 ng/ml Epidermal Growth Factor (EGF, Sigma, MA, United States). The cells were kept in a humidified incubator at 37 °C with a 5% CO2 atmosphere. For the cell assay, the cells were cultured in assay medium that included DMEM/F-12 medium with 5% horse serum, 0.5 µg/ml hydrocortisone, and 0.1 µg/ml cholera toxin to reduce the influence from insulin and EGF. Sample Preparation and Phosphoenrichment  For mass spectrometry experiments, ∼5 million cells were plated in triplicate in 10 cm plates in assay medium. After 24 h, assay medium with and without drugs was added. One group of the cells was incubated without drugs as a control, and six groups with drugs, including three drug conditions (10 µg/mL insulin, 500 nM alpelisib, and a combination), were incubated for 20 minutes and 60 minutes, respectively. Cells were washed three times with ice-cold PBS, scraped, and snap-frozen until further sample preparation.  For sample preparation, the SDC-based in-solution method was used as described previously. Cell pellets were lysed the lysis buffer, which consisted of 100 mM Tris, 10 mM TCEP, 40 mM chloroacetamide, a cOmplete mini EDTA-free tablet and PhosSTOP tablet, and 1% (w/v) sodium deoxycholate (SDC) in purified water. Subsequently, cells were boiled for 5 min at 95 °C and sonicated for 15 min at level 5 (30 s on, 30 s off, Bioruptor, model ACD-200, Diagenode, Liège, Belgium). Samples were diluted 1:10 using 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate before trypsin digestion (Sigma-Aldrich, MO, United States) using an enzyme: protein ratio of 1: 50 and overnight digestion at 37 °C. The tryptic peptides were acidified with formic acid (FA) at a final concentration of 2%. The peptides were centrifuged at 20,000 × g, and then the supernatant was collected and desalted using Sep-Pak C18 1 cc Vac cartridges (Waters, Reykjavik, Iceland). Peptides were vacuum-dried and stored at −80 °C before LC–MS analysis and phosphorylated peptides enrichment.  Phosphorylated peptides were enriched using Fe(III)-NTA 5 μL cartridges on the automated AssayMAP Bravo Platform (Agilent Technologies, CA, United States), as described previously.16,17 Samples were dissolved in 200 μL of loading buffer (80% acetonitrile/0.1% TFA), and Fe(III)-NTA cartridges were primed with 200 μL of 0.1% TFA in acetonitrile and equilibrated with 250 μL of loading buffer. The samples were loaded onto the column, and the column was washed with 250 μL of loading buffer. The phosphorylated peptides were eluted with 35 μL of 10% ammonia solution into 35 μL of 10% FA. Phosphopeptides were vacuum-dried and stored at −80 °C before LC–MS analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: Data-Independent Aquisiton of Proteome Data  Samples were suspended in 2% FA and analyzed on an Exploris 480 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to an UltiMate 3000 (Thermo Fisher Scientific), fitted with a μ-precolumn (C18 PepMap100, 5 μm, 100 Å, 5 mm × 300 μm; Thermo Fisher Scientific), and an analytical column (120 EC-C18, 2.7 μm, 50 cm × 75 μm; Agilent Poroshell). Samples were loaded in solvent A (0.1% FA in water) with a flow rate of 30 μL/min and eluted using a 115 min gradient at a flow rate of 300 nL/min. The gradient for peptides was as follows: 9% solvent B (0.1% FA in 80% acetonitrile, 20% water) for 1 min, 9–13% for 1 min, 13–44% for 95 min, 44–99% for 3 min, 99% for 4 min, 99–9% for 1 min, and finally the system equilibrated with 9% B for 10 min. The gradient for phosphopeptides was as follows: 9% solvent B for 1 min, 9–36% for 97 min, 36–99% for 3 min, 99% for 3 min, 99-9% for 1 min, and finally the system equilibrated with 9% B for 10 min. The mass spectrometer (MS) was operated in data independent acquisition mode, which consisted of an MS1 scan at 60,000 resolution at m/z with a scan range (m/z) of 375-1600. In master scan, the precursor mass range covered 400-1000 m/z with 30 sequential quadrupole isolation windows of 20 m/z and 1 m/z window overlap for HCD MS/MS. The detection of fragment ions in the Orbitrap (OT) was at 30,000 resolution, and the HCD collision energy was 28%. The Automatic Gain Control Target was set to standard and Maximum Injection Time Mode was set to auto for MS and MS/MS.  Spectra were extracted from the DIA data using DIA-NN (version 1.8.1) without a spectral library and with the “Deep learning” option enabled.18 The precursor false discovery rate threshold was set to 1%. The enzyme for digestion was set to trypsin, and the maximum number of missed cleavages was set to 2. Cysteine carbamidomethylation enabled as a fixed modification and the maximum number of variable modifications set to 2. All other settings were kept at the default values. Data-Dependent Aquisition of Phosphoproteome Data  Samples were suspended in 2% FA and analyzed on the same instruments and LC settings as proteomic samples. MS data were acquired in data-dependent acquisition (DDA) mode. The full scan MS spectra were acquired at a resolution of 60,000 within the m/z range of 375–1600 using a “Standard” preset automated gain control (AGC) target. MS2 scans were acquired with a 16 s dynamic exclusion at a 30000 resolution, 28% normalized collision energy, an AGC target set to standard, and an isolation window of 1.4 m/z. High-energy collision dissociation was performed with 28% normalized collision energy at an Orbitrap. Multiply charged precursor ions starting from m/z 120 were selected for further fragmentation.  The MS/MS spectra were searched by the Andromeda search engine against an in silico tryptic digest of Homo sapiens proteins from the UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot sequence database (version June 2023). The parameters of MaxQuant software version 2.4.2.0 (www.maxquant.net)19 were set as follows: cysteine carbamidomethylation as fixed modification and oxidized methionine, protein N-terminal acetylation, and serine/threonine/tyrosine phosphorylation as variable modifications; digestion by trypsin; and two maximum missed cleavages. The protein and peptide-spectrum match (PSM) false discovery rate was set to 1%. Label-free quantification (LFQ) was applied for quantification without matching between runs.
